source.title: Phasic locus coeruleus activity regulates cortical encoding of salience information
source.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

confidence_rationale: The only causal, cell-type-specific, phasic-versus-tonic manipulation in this pull: optogenetic phasic (not tonic) LC-NE activation produces a cortical ERP and lifts cortical responses to weak, non-salient stimuli to salient-stimulus levels when time-locked to the stimulus. That is close to MECH-084's required phasic-vs-tonic contrast and its 'pulse increases bottom-up weighting' prediction. Capped because it measures sensory encoding gain, not an allocation ratio between bottom-up and top-down, there is no top-down prediction to override, and it is anaesthetised/rodent physiology.
failure_signatures: The manipulation enhances the cortical response to a stimulus, but there is no established top-down prediction in the paradigm, so the result cannot distinguish 'NA increases bottom-up weight relative to top-down constraint' (MECH-084) from 'NA simply increases gain on whatever input arrives'.
No behavioural reorientation or latency measure is reported, so the orienting half of the claim is untested here.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Phasic, but not tonic, optogenetic activation of LC-NE neurons generates a distinct cortical event-related potential; weak non-salient stimuli that normally produce limited cortical responses are elevated to salient-stimulus response levels when temporally locked with phasic LC photoactivation, via facilitation of long-latency signals in target regions.
mapping.ree_translation: A causal demonstration that a phasic NA pulse, timed to an input, increases that input's weight in cortical encoding, while an equal tonic drive does not produce the same signature. In REE terms: the phasic channel, not mean NA level, is what transiently promotes a bottom-up E1 signal -- the 'snap' half of MECH-084, and a partial answer to the falsifier's 'matched mean NA with different temporal profile' control.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Gain on sensory encoding is not the same as an E1/E2 sampling-allocation ratio; there is no top-down expectation being overridden and no reorientation behaviour. The phasic/tonic contrast is by stimulation pattern, and is not formally matched for total NE release.
mapping.source_context: Rats; Cre-dependent optogenetic activation of LC-NE neurons with single-unit and field recordings in cortical targets; salient vs weak sensory stimuli.

confidence_components.notes: PNAS, cell-type-specific optogenetics with a phasic/tonic contrast -- the manipulation most like MECH-084's falsifier. Mapping held down because the DV is encoding gain, not an allocation ratio.
